official.citizenship_residency: For international applicants; no nationality restriction is published - the program has brought over 894 scholars from 115 countries to Brandeis since 1958
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the program exists specifically for international applicants to Brandeis undergraduate programs

official.description: The Wien International Scholarship Program (WISP) at Brandeis University, established in 1958, is a first-of-its-kind program bringing undergraduate students from every corner of the globe to campus and engaging the entire community to be active global citizens. It is a need-based scholarship that meets the full demonstrated financial need of each recipient, awarded to exceptional international applicants who show strong academic achievement and extracurricular or community involvement. Since its inception it has brought over 894 scholars from 115 countries to Brandeis.
official.program_type: Need-based institutional scholarship for international undergraduate students, awarded through the admission process
official.english_requirement: International applicants for whom English is not a native language should submit an English proficiency exam result: TOEFL iBT, IELTS, Duolingo English Test (DET, submitted directly by the testing agency), or Cambridge Assessment English C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency. Exempt with four or more years at a high school whose full academic curriculum is in English (waiver requested in the DEISconnect portal) or when applying directly from a United World College campus. No minimum scores are published.

applicant_utility.summary: The Wien International Scholarship is Brandeis' flagship need-based award for international undergraduates, and it is won through the admission application itself - there is no separate essay, portal, or deadline to chase. Your realistic move is to apply Early Decision I or Early Action (Nov. 2) if Brandeis is a genuine first choice, because the aid file is reviewed with that round and the award lands inside the admission letter. File the CSS Profile (Brandeis code 3092) at the same time as your admission application, not after, and be ready to back every income and asset figure with documents translated into English. Expect the award to meet your full calculated need rather than a headline number: families with means will see a package reduced by an expected family contribution, so build a realistic personal budget for the gap.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international students with real financial need, a record of community or extracurricular leadership, and a family that cannot pay full US private-university costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm Brandeis offers your intended major and that you can meet the Common App/Coalition App requirements (transcripts, school report, counselor and teacher recommendations)
Open the CSS Profile early and register both student and parent accounts - Brandeis code 3092 - since non-US income and asset fields take longer to complete than domestic ones
Collect documents proving the prior tax year's income: government tax returns or employer salary letters, plus bank and investment statements for savings and assets
Get certified English translations ready for any document not originally in English, from a consulate, embassy, or school official
If your parents are divorced or separated, plan for the extra Noncustodial Profile filing
Decide your round deliberately: ED I/EA (Nov. 2) gets an aid decision with admission, while ED II/RD (Jan. 15) is the last chance for Fall 2027 entry
common_rejection_risks: Forgetting to indicate intent to apply for financial aid on the admissions application - Brandeis states that after admission decisions are released you cannot apply for institutional aid
Filing the CSS Profile late or without supporting documentation, since late applications may not be considered
Missing the renewal filing on March 1 in later years - aid is re-determined annually and lapses if you skip it
Applying without English proficiency evidence when required, or without requesting the exemption waiver for four-plus years of English-medium schooling
Assuming a need-based award guarantees full cost of attendance when the family's calculated contribution still has to be funded
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any expected family contribution remains the family's responsibility, and Brandeis' published 2026-2027 cost sheet shows items outside the billed tuition/fee/housing/food lines: books and supplies $1,000, personal expenses $1,200, travel (varies), plus international-only charges - new student fee $635, international student fee $252 per semester, and the mandatory School Health Plan premium of $4,700 per year, to which all international students are automatically enrolled.
document_audit: Every financial document must be in English or carry a certified translation from a consulate, embassy, or school official - informal translations are a common stall point
If no business tax return was filed, Brandeis asks families to contact the financial aid office for alternate documentation rather than leaving the field blank
DET scores must come straight from Duolingo; TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge scans are accepted, so plan official reporting time around the deadline
Transcripts need certified English versions of the originals, covering all years of secondary school
Once the CSS Profile is submitted, corrections must be sent to Brandeis directly - you cannot simply edit and resubmit
alerts: Aid cannot be added later: institutional financial aid is only available to international students who receive it upon admittance
Renewal is conditional - maximum eight semesters, continued demonstrated need, satisfactory academic progress, and the required GPA
The renewal deadline (March 1) is much earlier than most students expect and arrives mid-second semester
Third-party interview recordings have their own cut-offs (Nov. 15 ED I; Jan. 15 ED II/RD), so book InitialView or Vericant slots well ahead
Watch for scams: Brandeis warns it never partners with external agents or organizations for Wien selection or aid processing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the admission application with the financial-aid intent box ticked, file the CSS Profile the same day, respond to any documentation requests, then wait for the admission decision - the Wien or other Brandeis scholarship notice arrives with it.
